```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(stringr)

```

# Purpose

Answers Reviewer 1's two statistical points **at the level the manuscript reports them** —
that is, collapsed across stimuli, which is how the paper is written and how the intervention
would be used clinically:

> "The claim that OPS eliminates sound-induced VS rests on comparing proportions across
> conditions (e.g., 60.5% vs. 81.6%; 18/23 elimination), yet no test (e.g., McNemar's test for
> paired proportions, chi-square tests, or Cochran's Q across the four phases) is performed to
> establish that these differences are not attributable to chance."

> "The comparison of DS vs. COS efficacy, and the analysis of concordance between anatomically
> equivalent stimulations (complete/partial/no concordance in 5/3/3 cases), are presented as
> raw counts with no measure of agreement (e.g., Cohen's kappa) or confidence intervals."

**Framing decision (Esther, 2026-08-17).** The collapsed proportions are computed and tested
as the clinical estimand: the question is whether *some* oral stimulus can be found for a
patient, and how many were tried is part of the protocol rather than a nuisance. That is a
coherent estimand and it is what the paper claims. `prevalence_ci_and_paired_contrasts.Rmd`
holds the per-stimulus analysis, which answers the different question of whether a *given*
stimulus works.

Retrospective and exploratory throughout. Nothing here was pre-specified.

```{r load}
proc <- file.path("..", "..", "data", "processed")
f <- file.path(proc, "participant_condition_long.csv")
if (!file.exists(f)) stop("Run collapse_conditions_and_classify.Rmd first.")

long <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
n_p <- n_distinct(long$pid)
stopifnot(nrow(long) == n_p * 23)

chk <- round(100 * wilson(23, 38), 1)
stopifnot(abs(chk[["lower"]] - 44.7) < 0.15, abs(chk[["upper"]] - 74.4) < 0.15)
cat("n =", n_p, "| Wilson verified against the plan's worked example\n")
```

# ⚠️ 1. The warning that has to travel with every number below

**The collapsed comparison gives the oral conditions more chances to be positive than the
sound condition, and the study did not repeat the sound condition to match.**

Concretely: "VS with OPS" is positive if *any* of 11 oral stimuli produced a VS in any of 12
drawings — up to 132 binary opportunities. "VS with sound" rests on **one** presentation of the
sound and 12 drawings. So part of the gap between 60.5% and 81.6% is the difference in how many
times each condition was sampled, not a difference between sound and oral stimulation.

The same asymmetry inflates the elimination endpoint: to be counted as eliminating, a
participant needed *one* of 11 stimuli to clear all 12 drawings, and the study never re-measured
sound-only to estimate how often the line comes back on its own.

**This cannot be corrected from the data on hand** — correcting it needs repeated sound-only
measurements, which is `ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` §2a.4 and open item 3 in `../../CLAUDE.md` (Clàudia's
thesis). It is recorded here so the limitation is on the record, identified by Esther on
2026-08-17, before any of these tests were read.

⚠️ **The reviewer did not raise this.** Whether to volunteer it in the response letter is
Esther's call — answering only what is asked is defensible. What is **not** defensible is
printing these comparisons in the paper without the limitation stated somewhere in it. It is
therefore tracked in `Manuscript/MANUSCRIPT.md` §4 as a limitation for the Limitations section,
not as a point in the reply.

```{r per-pid}
per_pid <- long |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(
    sound    = any_vs[block_type == "sound_only"],
    ops_snd  = as.integer(any(any_vs[block_type == "oral_plus_sound"] == 1)),
    # "OPS" in the paper means the oral-alone phase, E13-E23. Verified below: that reading
    # reproduces all five published cells (31 / 3 / 11 / 20 / 4); reading OPS as any oral
    # condition, or as oral + sound, reproduces none of them.
    ops      = as.integer(any(any_vs[block_type == "oral_alone"] == 1)),
    ops_alone= as.integer(any(any_vs[block_type == "oral_alone"] == 1)),
    elim_ds  = as.integer(any(classification[block_type == "oral_plus_sound" & type == "DS"]  == "regulador")),
    elim_cos = as.integer(any(classification[block_type == "oral_plus_sound" & type == "COS"] == "regulador")),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(elim_any = as.integer(elim_ds == 1 | elim_cos == 1))

# Reproduce the published counts before testing anything against them.
stopifnot(sum(per_pid$sound) == 23, sum(per_pid$ops) == 31)
stopifnot(sum(per_pid$sound == 0 & per_pid$ops == 0) == 4)
stopifnot(sum(per_pid$sound == 1 & per_pid$ops == 1) == 20)
stopifnot(sum(per_pid$sound == 1 & per_pid$ops == 0) == 3)
stopifnot(sum(per_pid$sound == 0 & per_pid$ops == 1) == 11)
stopifnot(sum(per_pid$elim_any) == 18)
cat("all published prevalence and elimination counts reproduce\n")
```

# 2. Every percentage in the paper, with its 95% Wilson interval

Transcribed from `Manuscript/drafts/…-EGH.docx`, Results §1–2 and the abstract. This is the
table the revision needs.

⚠️ Two things the paper's own arithmetic gets wrong, found while building this:

1. The text says *"Of these 34: 3 (7.9%), 11 (29.0%), 20 (52.6%)"* — but those three
   percentages are **of 38, not of 34**. Out of 34 they would be 8.8%, 32.4% and 58.8%. Either
   the denominator sentence or the percentages must change.
2. The elimination endpoint is printed as **47.3% (18/38)** in the abstract and Results. That
   is arithmetically right but it is the wrong denominator for the claim: the population at
   risk of *eliminating* a sound-induced VS is the 23 who had one, giving **78.3%**. Both are
   in the table; the paper should lead with 78.3% of 23 and may quote 47.3% of 38 as a
   secondary framing.

```{r percentages}
row_ci <- function(label, x, n, note = "") {
  ci <- wilson(x, n)
  tibble(quantity = label, x = x, n = n,
         pct = round(100 * x / n, 1),
         lower = round(100 * ci[["lower"]], 1),
         upper = round(100 * ci[["upper"]], 1),
         note = note)
}

paper_tbl <- bind_rows(
  row_ci("No VS under any condition",                sum(per_pid$sound == 0 & per_pid$ops == 0), 38),
  row_ci("VS under at least one condition",          sum(per_pid$sound == 1 | per_pid$ops == 1), 38),
  row_ci("VS with sound only",                       sum(per_pid$sound == 1 & per_pid$ops == 0), 38,
         "paper prints 7.9%, i.e. of 38, while the sentence says 'of these 34'"),
  row_ci("VS with OPS only",                         sum(per_pid$sound == 0 & per_pid$ops == 1), 38,
         "paper prints 29.0%, of 38, same issue"),
  row_ci("VS with both sound and OPS",               sum(per_pid$sound == 1 & per_pid$ops == 1), 38,
         "paper prints 52.6%, of 38, same issue"),
  row_ci("VS during sound stimulation",              sum(per_pid$sound), 38),
  row_ci("VS during OPS",                            sum(per_pid$ops), 38,
         "union over the 11 oral-alone conditions, phase 4 - see section 1"),
  row_ci("Elimination of sound-induced VS, of the 23 at risk", sum(per_pid$elim_any), 23,
         "the correct denominator for the claim"),
  row_ci("Elimination of sound-induced VS, of all 38",         sum(per_pid$elim_any), 38,
         "the paper's 47.3% - arithmetically right, wrong denominator for the claim"),
  row_ci("Of the 23: eliminated by DS (alone or with COS)",    sum(per_pid$elim_ds), 23),
  row_ci("Of the 23: eliminated by COS (alone or with DS)",    sum(per_pid$elim_cos), 23),
  row_ci("Of the 23: eliminated by DS only",  sum(per_pid$elim_ds == 1 & per_pid$elim_cos == 0), 23),
  row_ci("Of the 23: eliminated by COS only", sum(per_pid$elim_ds == 0 & per_pid$elim_cos == 1), 23),
  row_ci("Of the 23: eliminated by both",     sum(per_pid$elim_ds == 1 & per_pid$elim_cos == 1), 23),
  # must be restricted to the 23: elim_any == 0 is also true for all 15 who had no
  # sound-induced VS to eliminate, and counting those against a denominator of 23 gives 20/23.
  row_ci("Of the 23: no elimination",
         sum(per_pid$sound == 1 & per_pid$elim_any == 0), 23)
)

# The four elimination outcomes must partition the 23 exactly.
stopifnot(sum(per_pid$elim_ds == 1 & per_pid$elim_cos == 0) +
          sum(per_pid$elim_ds == 0 & per_pid$elim_cos == 1) +
          sum(per_pid$elim_ds == 1 & per_pid$elim_cos == 1) +
          sum(per_pid$sound == 1 & per_pid$elim_any == 0) == 23)

knitr::kable(paper_tbl, caption = "Every proportion the manuscript reports, with 95% Wilson intervals")
```

# 3. Sound vs OPS — the 60.5% vs 81.6% the reviewer names

These are **paired** proportions: the same 38 people contributed both. A chi-square test would
be wrong here, because it assumes two independent samples and would use the wrong standard
error. Exact McNemar is the correct test and is what the reviewer's own first suggestion names.

⚠️ **Note which phases this compares.** Reproducing the published cells establishes that the
paper's "OPS" in the prevalence section means the **oral-alone phase (phase 4)**, not oral +
sound. So 60.5% vs 81.6% is *sound alone* against *oral stimuli with the sound off* — two
isolated conditions from two different phases. The elimination endpoint, by contrast, uses
**phase 3** (oral + sound). The paper calls both "OPS", which is a clarity problem the revision
should fix regardless of what any test returns.

```{r sound-vs-ops}
tab <- with(per_pid, c(
  a = sum(sound == 1 & ops == 1), b = sum(sound == 1 & ops == 0),
  c = sum(sound == 0 & ops == 1), d = sum(sound == 0 & ops == 0)))
print(tab)

mc <- mcnemar_exact(tab[["b"]], tab[["c"]])
nc <- newcombe_paired(tab[["a"]], tab[["b"]], tab[["c"]], tab[["d"]])

cat(sprintf("\nVS with sound   : %d/38 = %.1f%%\n", tab[["a"]] + tab[["b"]],
            100 * (tab[["a"]] + tab[["b"]]) / 38))
cat(sprintf("VS with OPS     : %d/38 = %.1f%%\n", tab[["a"]] + tab[["c"]],
            100 * (tab[["a"]] + tab[["c"]]) / 38))
cat(sprintf("Risk difference : %+.1f pp [%+.1f, %+.1f]  (negative = OPS higher)\n",
            100 * nc[["rd"]], 100 * nc[["lower"]], 100 * nc[["upper"]]))
cat(sprintf("Exact McNemar   : p = %.4f  on %d discordant pairs (b=%d, c=%d)\n",
            mc[["p"]], mc[["discordant"]], tab[["b"]], tab[["c"]]))
```

**Reading.** The difference is in the direction of *more* VS under OPS, not less, and it is
statistically clear. But it is the least interesting significant result in the study: §1 says
the OPS arm had up to 132 opportunities against the sound arm's 12, so this test largely
confirms that more sampling finds more events. **It should not be reported as evidence that
oral stimulation induces more pseudo-scotomas than sound.** The honest use of this number is
descriptive — 81.6% of participants showed a VS somewhere in the oral protocol.

# 4. Cochran's Q across phases

The reviewer asks for Q across four phases. Two obstacles, both worth stating in the reply:

1. **Phase 1 is not in the data file.** The 0/38 is an assertion (Esther, 2026-08-17), not a
   recorded column. Entering it as a constant column of zeros would make Q partly a test
   against a number that cannot be checked, and a constant column inflates Q mechanically.
2. **The phases are not comparable in opportunity** — phase 2 is one condition, phases 3 and 4
   are unions of eleven each (§1). Q would then be measuring the number of chances each phase
   had, not the effect of its stimulus.

Q is therefore reported across the **three measurable phases**, with the caveat attached, and
`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` §5 keeps the per-stimulus model as the analysis that answers the question
properly.

```{r cochran}
X <- as.matrix(per_pid[, c("sound", "ops_snd", "ops_alone")])
colnames(X) <- c("Sound alone", "Oral + sound (any)", "Oral alone (any)")
print(colSums(X))

q3 <- cochran_q(X)
cat(sprintf("\nCochran's Q = %.3f, df = %d, p = %.4f  (%d informative participants)\n",
            q3[["Q"]], q3[["df"]], q3[["p"]], q3[["informative_rows"]]))

# What adding the asserted all-zero baseline would do, for the record only.
q4 <- cochran_q(cbind(baseline = 0L, X))
cat(sprintf("With the asserted 0/38 baseline as a 4th column: Q = %.3f, df = %d, p = %.5f\n",
            q4[["Q"]], q4[["df"]], q4[["p"]]))
cat("\nThe 4-phase Q is larger purely because a column that is 0 for everyone cannot agree\n",
    "with columns where most people are positive. It is not evidence about the stimuli.\n")
```

# 5. DS vs COS efficacy

Among the 23 participants with a sound-induced VS, did dental stimuli and combined oral stimuli
differ in how often they eliminated it? Paired again — the same 23 people were exposed to both.

```{r ds-vs-cos}
sub <- filter(per_pid, sound == 1)
stopifnot(nrow(sub) == 23)

t2 <- with(sub, c(a = sum(elim_ds == 1 & elim_cos == 1), b = sum(elim_ds == 1 & elim_cos == 0),
                  c = sum(elim_ds == 0 & elim_cos == 1), d = sum(elim_ds == 0 & elim_cos == 0)))
print(t2)
# must match the published 11 both / 5 DS only / 2 COS only
stopifnot(t2[["a"]] == 11, t2[["b"]] == 5, t2[["c"]] == 2)

mc2 <- mcnemar_exact(t2[["b"]], t2[["c"]])
nc2 <- newcombe_paired(t2[["a"]], t2[["b"]], t2[["c"]], t2[["d"]])
w_ds  <- wilson(t2[["a"]] + t2[["b"]], 23)
w_cos <- wilson(t2[["a"]] + t2[["c"]], 23)

cat(sprintf("\nEliminated by DS  : %d/23 = %.1f%% [%.1f, %.1f]\n", t2[["a"]] + t2[["b"]],
            100 * (t2[["a"]] + t2[["b"]]) / 23, 100 * w_ds[["lower"]], 100 * w_ds[["upper"]]))
cat(sprintf("Eliminated by COS : %d/23 = %.1f%% [%.1f, %.1f]\n", t2[["a"]] + t2[["c"]],
            100 * (t2[["a"]] + t2[["c"]]) / 23, 100 * w_cos[["lower"]], 100 * w_cos[["upper"]]))
cat(sprintf("Risk difference   : %+.1f pp [%+.1f, %+.1f]  (positive = DS more often)\n",
            100 * nc2[["rd"]], 100 * nc2[["lower"]], 100 * nc2[["upper"]]))
cat(sprintf("Exact McNemar     : p = %.4f  on only %d discordant pairs\n",
            mc2[["p"]], mc2[["discordant"]]))
```

⚠️ **Seven discordant pairs.** Whatever this test returns, it cannot distinguish anything but a
very large difference. The interval is the honest answer, and it is wide. Note also that DS had
**8 stimuli and COS only 3**, so DS again had more chances — the same §1 problem inside this
comparison. That is a further reason the point estimate favouring DS should not be read as DS
being the better stimulus type.

# 6. Agreement between DS and COS — the reviewer's kappa

Two different agreement questions. Both are reported because the reviewer's wording spans them.

## 6a. Do DS and COS agree about *whose* sound-induced VS they eliminated? (n = 23)

The 2x2 below is the published 11 both / 5 DS-only / 2 COS-only, plus the 5 who eliminated with
neither. Agreement = both eliminated, or neither did. The denominator is the 23 who had a
sound-induced VS, not the 18 who eliminated: elimination is only a question for someone who had
one, and restricting to the 18 would empty cell `d` so kappa could not be computed.

⚠️ Do **not** describe this as "responding to both stimulus types" — it is specifically about
elimination of a sound-induced VS, and the vaguer phrasing reads as something else.

```{r kappa-elim}
k1 <- kappa_2x2(t2[["a"]], t2[["b"]], t2[["c"]], t2[["d"]])
print(round(k1, 3))
cat(sprintf("\nraw agreement %.1f%% [%.1f, %.1f] | kappa %.2f [%.2f, %.2f] | PABAK %.2f\n",
            100 * k1[["po"]], 100 * k1[["po_lower"]], 100 * k1[["po_upper"]],
            k1[["kappa"]], k1[["kappa_lower"]], k1[["kappa_upper"]], k1[["pabak"]]))
```

**This is the prevalence/bias paradox the plan predicted, now with numbers.** Raw agreement is
high while kappa is modest, because elimination is common in this subgroup — the prevalence
index is large, so chance agreement is high and kappa is pulled down. Reporting kappa alone
would understate the agreement; reporting raw agreement alone would overstate it. Report both,
plus PABAK, and say why they differ. The kappa interval is a large-sample approximation at
n = 23 and should be described as indicative only.

## 6b. Concordance between anatomically equivalent stimulations (n = 11)

✅ **RESOLVED 2026-08-17. The published 5 complete / 3 partial / 3 none now reproduces exactly.**

The definition was read off the draft by Esther (Results ¶178 plus the Fig. 2 equivalences) and is:

- Each of the **three** COS slots (M1, M2, M3) is judged for every participant — including slots
  where that COS did **not** eliminate.
- A slot **matches** if the COS eliminated **and at least one** of its anatomically equivalent DS
  eliminated. "At least one", not all — that was the piece I had wrong.
- **complete** = all 3 slots match · **partial** = 1 or 2 match · **none** = 0 match.

Equivalences, Fig. 2: M1 ↔ 11P, 21P · M2 ↔ 11V, 21V, 31V, 41V · M3 ↔ 31L, 41L.

⚠️ **This is positive co-occurrence, not two-way agreement.** A slot where neither the COS nor its
equivalents eliminated counts as a **non-match** here, whereas an agreement statistic such as
kappa would count it as agreement. That is why the classification below and the kappa further down
are different quantities and must not be presented as the same thing measured twice.

❓ **UNCONFIRMED, and it is the one judgement call left in this analysis.** Treating "neither
eliminated" as a non-match is what reproduces 5/3/3, so it is almost certainly what the authors
did — but it has not been confirmed by them. The alternative convention (count it as concordant,
i.e. reading E below) gives **5/5/1**, moving two participants from `none` to `partial`. Asked of
Sophie in `Manuscript/revisions/analysis_summary.md` §3e and §6. If she confirms the *other*
convention, `published` must be replaced by `reading_E` and the assertion below updated.

The three earlier readings that failed are kept in the code so the search is on the record.

```{r concordance}
elim <- long |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  transmute(pid, oral, elim = as.integer(classification == "regulador"))

equiv <- list(M1 = c("11P", "21P"),
              M2 = c("11V", "21V", "31V", "41V"),
              M3 = c("31L", "41L"))

got <- function(p, s) any(elim$elim[elim$pid == p & elim$oral %in% s] == 1)

both_types <- filter(per_pid, elim_ds == 1, elim_cos == 1)$pid
stopifnot(length(both_types) == 11)

n_eq_elim <- function(p, m) sum(elim$elim[elim$pid == p & elim$oral %in% equiv[[m]]] == 1)

conc <- lapply(both_types, function(p) {
  cos_used <- vapply(names(equiv), function(m) got(p, m), logical(1))
  any_ds   <- vapply(names(equiv), function(m) n_eq_elim(p, m) >= 1, logical(1))
  all_ds   <- vapply(names(equiv), function(m) n_eq_elim(p, m) == length(equiv[[m]]),
                     logical(1))
  used <- which(cos_used)
  tibble(
    pid = p, n_cos = sum(cos_used),
    n_matched = sum(any_ds[used]),
    # A: only the COS the participant actually eliminated with are judged; a COS counts as
    #    matched if ANY of its anatomical equivalents eliminated.
    reading_A = if (length(used) == 0) "none"
                else if (all(any_ds[used])) "complete"
                else if (any(any_ds[used])) "partial" else "none",
    # C: as A, but "complete" demands that ALL equivalents of each used COS eliminated.
    reading_C = if (length(used) == 0) "none"
                else if (all(all_ds[used])) "complete"
                else if (any(any_ds[used])) "partial" else "none",
    # E: all THREE COS slots are judged, in both directions - the COS and its equivalent DS
    #    must agree on eliminating or on not eliminating. This is the reading that treats
    #    "concordance" as agreement rather than as co-occurrence.
    agree3 = sum(cos_used == any_ds),
    reading_E = if (sum(cos_used == any_ds) == 3) "complete"
                else if (sum(cos_used == any_ds) == 0) "none" else "partial",
    # ===== THE PUBLISHED DEFINITION =====
    # All three COS slots judged; a slot matches iff the COS eliminated AND >= 1 of its
    # anatomical equivalents eliminated. complete = 3 matches, partial = 1-2, none = 0.
    n_match   = sum(cos_used & any_ds),
    published = if (sum(cos_used & any_ds) == 3) "complete"
                else if (sum(cos_used & any_ds) == 0) "none" else "partial"
  )
}) |> bind_rows()

knitr::kable(conc, caption = "Per participant: n_match / published is the reproduced rule; readings A, C and E are the earlier attempts that failed")

for (r in c("published", "reading_A", "reading_C", "reading_E")) {
  cat("\n", r, ":\n", sep = ""); print(table(factor(conc[[r]],
      levels = c("complete", "partial", "none"))))
}
cat("\nPaper reports: complete 5 / partial 3 / none 3\n")

# The reproduced rule must keep reproducing, or something upstream has changed.
pub <- table(factor(conc$published, levels = c("complete", "partial", "none")))
stopifnot(pub[["complete"]] == 5, pub[["partial"]] == 3, pub[["none"]] == 3)
cat("\n*** 5 / 3 / 3 REPRODUCED - asserted, so this knit fails if it ever stops holding ***\n")

cat("\nParticipant-level proportions with 95% Wilson intervals (n = 11):\n")
for (cl in c("complete", "partial", "none")) {
  x <- sum(conc$published == cl); ci <- wilson(x, nrow(conc))
  cat(sprintf("  %-9s %2d/%d = %4.1f%%  [%4.1f, %4.1f]\n", cl, x, nrow(conc),
              100 * x / nrow(conc), 100 * ci[["lower"]], 100 * ci[["upper"]]))
}

count_reading <- function(r) {
  tt <- table(factor(conc[[r]], levels = c("complete", "partial", "none")))
  tibble(source = paste("rebuild,", r), complete = tt[["complete"]],
         partial = tt[["partial"]], none = tt[["none"]])
}

summary_tbl <- bind_rows(
  tibble(source = "manuscript draft, Results para 178", complete = 5, partial = 3, none = 3),
  tibble(source = "Spanish recount",                    complete = 5, partial = 3, none = 3),
  tibble(source = "reviewer's letter",                  complete = 5, partial = 3, none = 3),
  count_reading("published"),
  count_reading("reading_A"), count_reading("reading_C"), count_reading("reading_E")
)
knitr::kable(summary_tbl, caption = "Concordance: what each source says")
```

### Worked examples, one per class

```{r concordance-examples}
show_pid <- function(p) {
  w <- filter(conc, pid == p)
  cat(sprintf("\nparticipant %s - %s (%d of 3 slots match)\n", p, w$published, w$n_match))
  for (m in names(equiv)) {
    cat(sprintf("  %-3s eliminated: %-3s | equivalents %-22s %d of %d eliminated | match: %s\n",
        m, if (got(p, m)) "YES" else "no", paste(equiv[[m]], collapse = ","),
        n_eq_elim(p, m), length(equiv[[m]]),
        if (got(p, m) && n_eq_elim(p, m) >= 1) "YES" else "NO"))
  }
}
for (cl in c("complete", "partial", "none")) show_pid(conc$pid[conc$published == cl][1])
```

```{r concordance-kappa}
# Agreement per COS-DS anatomical pair, pooled over the 11 participants. This is the
# defensible kappa for "do anatomically equivalent stimulations agree": one row per
# participant x COS type, agreement between the COS result and its equivalent DS result.
pair_dat <- expand_grid(pid = both_types, cos = names(equiv)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(cos_elim = as.integer(got(pid, cos)),
         ds_elim  = as.integer(got(pid, equiv[[cos]]))) |>
  ungroup()

t3 <- c(a = sum(pair_dat$cos_elim == 1 & pair_dat$ds_elim == 1),
        b = sum(pair_dat$cos_elim == 1 & pair_dat$ds_elim == 0),
        c = sum(pair_dat$cos_elim == 0 & pair_dat$ds_elim == 1),
        d = sum(pair_dat$cos_elim == 0 & pair_dat$ds_elim == 0))
print(t3)

# Two DIFFERENT quantities from the same table, and the distinction matters:
#   positive concordance = of the slots where the COS eliminated, how many had an equivalent
#                          DS eliminate too. This is what the paper's 5/3/3 is built from.
#   two-way agreement    = a + d, counting "neither eliminated" as agreement. This is what
#                          kappa is built from.
pc <- wilson(t3[["a"]], t3[["a"]] + t3[["b"]])
cat(sprintf("\nPOSITIVE CONCORDANCE: of the %d slots where the COS eliminated, %d also had at\n",
            t3[["a"]] + t3[["b"]], t3[["a"]]))
cat(sprintf("  least one equivalent DS eliminate = %.1f%% [%.1f, %.1f]\n",
            100 * t3[["a"]] / (t3[["a"]] + t3[["b"]]),
            100 * pc[["lower"]], 100 * pc[["upper"]]))
cat("  ^ this is the quantity the published 5/3/3 classification rests on.\n")

k2 <- kappa_2x2(t3[["a"]], t3[["b"]], t3[["c"]], t3[["d"]])
cat(sprintf("\nTWO-WAY AGREEMENT over %d anatomical pairs from %d participants\n",
            sum(t3), length(both_types)))
cat("  (counts the", t3[["d"]], "slots where NEITHER eliminated as agreement)\n")
cat(sprintf("raw agreement %.1f%% [%.1f, %.1f] | kappa %.2f [%.2f, %.2f] | PABAK %.2f\n",
            100 * k2[["po"]], 100 * k2[["po_lower"]], 100 * k2[["po_upper"]],
            k2[["kappa"]], k2[["kappa_lower"]], k2[["kappa_upper"]], k2[["pabak"]]))
cat("\nTHREE LIMITS on this number, all reported alongside it:\n")
cat("1. 'any equivalent DS eliminated' is not an even bar across rows: M2 has FOUR equivalents\n",
    "   (11V,21V,31V,41V) while M1 and M3 have two. The M2 row's DS side therefore has twice\n",
    "   the chances of coming out positive - the opportunity asymmetry again, inside this table.\n")
cat("2. The COS margin is constrained by selection. The 11 were chosen for eliminating with\n",
    "   BOTH types, so each must have >=1 COS eliminating among their 3 rows.\n")
cat(sprintf("   observed COS-positive rows: %d of %d (arithmetic minimum %d)\n",
            t3[["a"]] + t3[["b"]], sum(t3), length(both_types)))
cat("3. The 33 pairs are 3 per participant, so they are NOT independent. This kappa ignores\n",
    "   that clustering and its interval is therefore too narrow.\n")
cat("\nReported because the reviewer asked for kappa. Descriptive only; the per-participant\n",
    "classification above is the honest unit of analysis.\n")
```

# 7. The elimination endpoint against a reference rate

**Decision (Esther, 2026-08-17): report an exact binomial test of 18/23 against a reference
rate of 0.50, explicitly labelled exploratory, with the limitation stated.**

Why this rather than McNemar. Restricted to the 23 participants who had a sound-induced VS,
prevalence under sound is **100% by selection**, so the paired 2×2 has c = 0 forced — nobody in
that subgroup could get worse in this coding. McNemar then reduces to p = 2/2^b, which makes any
6 or more eliminators automatically significant regardless of what the stimuli did. A one-sample
test against an external reference has no such degeneracy: the null lives outside the data.

```{r elimination-degenerate}
elig <- filter(per_pid, sound == 1)
b_deg <- sum(elig$elim_any == 1); c_deg <- sum(elig$sound == 0)
cat(sprintf("within the 23: b = %d, c = %d (forced), McNemar p = %.3g  <- degenerate\n",
            b_deg, c_deg, binom.test(b_deg, b_deg + c_deg, 0.5)$p.value))
cat("   with c = 0 this is 2/2^b, so >= 6 eliminators is always p < .05. Not reported.\n")
```

## The test as reported

Interval is **Wilson**, for consistency with every other proportion in this project
(`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` analysis 2). The test is the **exact binomial**. Note these come from
different families — a score interval and an exact test — so at the margin they could in
principle disagree; here they agree, since the interval excludes 0.50 and p < .05.

```{r elimination-test}
x_el <- sum(per_pid$elim_any); n_el <- sum(per_pid$sound)
bt   <- binom.test(x_el, n_el, 0.5)
w_el <- wilson(x_el, n_el)

cat(sprintf("Elimination of sound-induced VS: %d/%d = %.1f%%\n", x_el, n_el, 100*x_el/n_el))
cat(sprintf("  95%% Wilson CI          : [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]   <- reported\n",
            100*w_el[["lower"]], 100*w_el[["upper"]]))
cat(sprintf("  95%% Clopper-Pearson    : [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]   (for reference only)\n",
            100*bt$conf.int[1], 100*bt$conf.int[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Exact binomial vs 0.50 : p = %.4f\n", bt$p.value))
cat(sprintf("  Cohen's g              : %.3f\n", abs(x_el/n_el - 0.5)))
```

## The same endpoint, stimulus by stimulus

The claim is about eliminating a sound-induced pseudo-scotoma, so the population is the 23 who
had one and the question per stimulus is: **of those 23, how many did this stimulus clear?**
This keeps the endpoint and the denominator identical to the collapsed analysis above and only
changes how many stimuli are allowed to count — which is the comparison that matters for
deciding whether the finding is about oral stimulation in general or about a person-specific
search.

Note this is **not** the sound-vs-sound+oral paired contrast. That contrast counts participants
who acquired a pseudo-scotoma as well as those who lost one, and the 15 who never reacted to
sound are not part of this claim. It is retained in
`prevalence_ci_and_paired_contrasts.Rmd` as a secondary analysis of a broader question.

```{r per-stimulus-elimination}
reg_by_stim <- long |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  group_by(oral, type) |>
  summarise(x = sum(classification == "regulador"), .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(n = n_el,
         pct    = 100 * x / n,
         lower  = 100 * wilson(x, n)[["lower"]],
         upper  = 100 * wilson(x, n)[["upper"]],
         p_vs50 = binom.test(x, n, 0.5)$p.value) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Eleven tests on the same 23 people, so the family needs a multiplicity correction.
  # Benjamini-Hochberg rather than Bonferroni: these are repeated measurements on one sample,
  # so the tests are correlated and Bonferroni's independence assumption over-corrects.
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_vs50, method = "BH")) |>
  arrange(desc(pct))

knitr::kable(reg_by_stim, digits = c(0,0,0,0,1,1,1,4,4),
             caption = paste0("Elimination of sound-induced VS by each stimulus separately, out of the same ",
                              n_el, " participants. p_vs50 is the exact binomial test against the 0.50 ",
                              "reference; p_bh applies Benjamini-Hochberg across the eleven."))

cat(sprintf("\nbefore correction, stimuli with p < .05 : %d of %d\n",
            sum(reg_by_stim$p_vs50 < 0.05), nrow(reg_by_stim)))
cat(sprintf("after Benjamini-Hochberg, p < .05      : %d of %d\n",
            sum(reg_by_stim$p_bh < 0.05), nrow(reg_by_stim)))
cat(sprintf("smallest adjusted p                    : %.3f\n", min(reg_by_stim$p_bh)))

cat(sprintf("\nbest single stimulus : %s, %d/%d = %.1f%%\n",
            reg_by_stim$oral[1], reg_by_stim$x[1], n_el, reg_by_stim$pct[1]))
cat(sprintf("worst single stimulus: %s, %d/%d = %.1f%%\n",
            tail(reg_by_stim$oral,1), tail(reg_by_stim$x,1), n_el, tail(reg_by_stim$pct,1)))
cat(sprintf("any of the eleven    : %d/%d = %.1f%%\n", x_el, n_el, 100*x_el/n_el))
cat(sprintf("stimuli reaching p < .05 against the 50%% reference: %d of %d",
            sum(reg_by_stim$p_vs50 < 0.05), nrow(reg_by_stim)))
cat(sprintf("  (all of them BELOW 50%%, not above: %s)\n",
            paste(reg_by_stim$oral[reg_by_stim$p_vs50 < 0.05], collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("stimuli exceeding 50%%: %d of %d\n",
            sum(reg_by_stim$pct > 50), nrow(reg_by_stim)))
```

**This is the key comparison for the Discussion.** No single stimulus comes close to the
collapsed figure: the best is 31V at 12/23 = 52.2% [33.0, 70.8], and three (11V, 21P, 21V) sit
significantly **below** the 50% reference at 26.1%. Only one of the eleven exceeds 50% at all, and
not detectably so (p = 1.00).

So the 78.3% is produced by allowing *any* of eleven stimuli to count. **That makes it a claim
about a person-specific search — that for most people some stimulus can be found — rather than a
claim that oral proprioceptive stimulation has a general effect.** Both are defensible; only the
first is supported.

## ⚠️ The limitation, quantified

The reference value of 0.50 is a **convention, not an empirical no-effect rate.** Because the
sound-only condition was presented once, the rate at which a sound-induced VS would clear
spontaneously on re-testing is not estimable from these data (§2a.4). Two things show how much
turns on it.

**First, where the result changes.** The same 18/23 tested against other reference rates:

```{r benchmark-sensitivity}
bench <- data.frame(reference = c(.30, .40, .50, .56, .60, .65, .70, .80)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(p = binom.test(x_el, n_el, reference)$p.value,
         significant = ifelse(p < 0.05, "yes", "no")) |>
  ungroup()
knitr::kable(bench, digits = 4,
             caption = "Exact binomial test of 18/23 against a range of reference rates")
```

**Second, what a lenient endpoint plus eleven attempts can produce on its own.** Most of the 23
had only a few of the 12 drawings affected, and "elimination" needed just one of 11 stimuli to
clear all of them. If the reports were unrelated to the stimulus, with *q* the chance an
affected drawing reads clear on a re-read:

```{r noise-illustration}
k_burden <- long |> filter(block_type == "sound_only", any_vs == 1) |> pull(n_im)
cat("drawings affected under sound, among the 23:\n"); print(table(k_burden))
cat(sprintf("median %.0f of 12; %d of %d had only 1-2 affected\n\n",
            median(k_burden), sum(k_burden <= 2), length(k_burden)))

noise <- data.frame(q = c(.10, .20, .30, .40, .50)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(expected_elimination_pct = round(100 * mean(1 - (1 - q^k_burden)^11), 1)) |>
  ungroup()
knitr::kable(noise,
             caption = "Expected 'elimination' rate with NO stimulus effect, by per-drawing instability q")
```

Assumes independence across drawings and across conditions; positive within-condition
correlation would push these higher, since one clean trial clears everything at once. **At
q = 0.5 the no-effect rate is already ~59%, above the 0.50 being tested against.** That is the
substance of the limitation, and it is why this analysis is exploratory.

## Wording for the manuscript and the reply

Drafted here so the same phrasing is used in both. Esther to edit.

> **Limitations.** The proportion of participants in whom oral proprioceptive stimulation
> eliminated the sound-induced pseudo-scotoma (18/23; 78.3%, 95% CI 58.1–90.3%) was compared
> against a reference value of 50% using an exact binomial test (*p* = .011). This reference is
> a conventional benchmark rather than an empirically established one: because the sound-only
> condition was presented once, the rate at which a sound-induced pseudo-scotoma resolves
> spontaneously on re-testing could not be estimated in this study. This analysis is therefore
> exploratory. The confidence interval indicates that the observed rate is **not compatible with
> a spontaneous resolution rate below approximately 56%, but is fully compatible with rates of
> 60% or above.** Establishing the spontaneous resolution rate — for example by presenting the
> sound-only condition repeatedly within a session — would be necessary before this finding
> could be attributed specifically to oral proprioceptive stimulation.

For the response letter, shorter:

> We have added an exact binomial test of the elimination proportion against a 50% reference
> value (18/23; 78.3%, 95% CI 58.1–90.3%; *p* = .011), together with Wilson confidence intervals
> for all reported proportions and McNemar's test for the paired condition comparisons. We note
> explicitly that the 50% reference is conventional rather than empirical, since the sound-only
> condition was presented once and the spontaneous resolution rate could not be estimated; the
> analysis is presented as exploratory and this limitation is now stated in the Discussion.

dir.create(tab_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

collapsed <- tibble(
  comparison = c("Sound vs OPS (any)", "DS vs COS elimination, of the 23"),
  p1 = c(100 * (tab[["a"]] + tab[["b"]]) / 38, 100 * (t2[["a"]] + t2[["b"]]) / 23),
  p2 = c(100 * (tab[["a"]] + tab[["c"]]) / 38, 100 * (t2[["a"]] + t2[["c"]]) / 23),
  rd = c(100 * nc[["rd"]], 100 * nc2[["rd"]]),
  rd_lower = c(100 * nc[["lower"]], 100 * nc2[["lower"]]),
  rd_upper = c(100 * nc[["upper"]], 100 * nc2[["upper"]]),

)
write.csv(collapsed, file.path(tab_dir, "collapsed_comparisons.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

kappa_row <- function(label, k) data.frame(analysis = label, as.list(round(k, 4)),
                                          check.names = FALSE)
write.csv(
  rbind(kappa_row("DS vs COS elimination (n=23 participants)", k1),
        kappa_row("COS vs equivalent DS (anatomical pairs, clustered)", k2)),
  file.path(tab_dir, "agreement_kappa.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(summary_tbl, file.path(tab_dir, "concordance_readings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(
  data.frame(
    x = x_el, n = n_el, pct = round(100 * x_el / n_el, 1),
    wilson_lower = round(100 * w_el[["lower"]], 1),
    wilson_upper = round(100 * w_el[["upper"]], 1),

    cp_upper = round(100 * bt$conf.int[2], 1),

    status = "exploratory - reference rate is conventional, not empirical"
  ),
  file.path(tab_dir, "elimination_benchmark.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(bench,  file.path(tab_dir, "elimination_benchmark_sensitivity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(noise,  file.path(tab_dir, "elimination_noise_illustration.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(

             p = c(q3[["p"]], q4[["p"]]),

                      "includes the asserted all-zero baseline - inflated, for the record only")),
